headline: A 2022 law limits when federal leases can include bargain-price options to buy federal buildings below fair market value.
what_it_does: The law changes the rules for leases of federal buildings. A lease may include an option to buy the property for less than fair market value, but that option can be used only if a later act of Congress specifically allows it. The rule covers lease agreements signed on or after January 1, 2021.

who_it_affects.group: General Services Administration and other federal agencies that lease buildings
who_it_affects.how: They may not exercise a bargain-price purchase option in a federal building lease unless Congress has specifically provided for it in a later law.

who_it_affects.group: Private property owners who lease buildings to the federal government
who_it_affects.how: Leases signed on or after January 1, 2021 with bargain-price purchase options can be exercised only if Congress has specifically authorized them.

when_it_takes_effect: The rule applies to lease agreements entered into on or after January 1, 2021, and the law was enacted on December 21, 2022.
